segments.say: Let's look in on Ben one last time. It's Friday night now, the night before the wedding. And something unusual is happening. Ben is going to bed early. On the bedside table, there's a single printed page, folded neatly in half. The speech. It isn't perfect, but it's warm and true, and it's finished. He wrote it in small pieces, all through the week.

Picture that little page on the bedside table, folded in half, beside a glass of water and a small lamp. It holds a cape, a bicycle, and a family dinner full of laughter. It holds a brother's love for his sister. And it got written not by force, but by small, kind steps. Tonight, it can rest. And so can Ben.

show.cap: A finished page, ready for tomorrow

segments.say: Ben switches off the lamp. There's no last-minute rush tonight, no frantic typing at two in the morning. Just a dark, quiet room, a soft pillow, and a feeling of calm that he hasn't had for a while. He thinks of Clara, and smiles. And then, slowly, his thoughts begin to blur and drift, the way thoughts do just before sleep.

It's a gentle reminder for all of us. A small step each day can carry a big thing home. You don't need to do everything at once. You don't need to be fearless. You just need to take a little step, and then another, and be kind to yourself along the way. And then, when the night comes, you can rest with an easy heart.

show.text: A small step each day can carry a big thing home.

segments.say: Now let your mind drift out of the town, into the quiet countryside. Imagine wide, open fields under a clear night sky. The grass is soft and silvery in the moonlight. A low stone wall runs along the edge of a meadow. Somewhere, sheep are sleeping in a huddle. And the whole land is resting, breathing slowly, beneath the stars.

Imagine lying on a thick, soft blanket in the middle of the meadow. The grass beneath you is cool and springy. The air smells of hay and wildflowers. And above you, the sky stretches from one edge of the world to the other, deep and dark and full of quiet stars. You feel very small, and very safe, held between the earth and the sky.

Let's gather the gentle things around you. Soft grass, cool beneath your blanket. Sheep, sleeping in a warm huddle across the field. An old stone wall, holding the edge of the meadow. Cool night air, smelling of hay and flowers. And endless stars, scattered across the sky. Everything here is resting. And you can rest too.

As you watch, a shooting star slides slowly across the sky, a thin line of light, and then it's gone. You don't need to make a wish. You don't need to do anything at all. You can just notice it, and let it go, the way you've been letting go of the day, one small thing at a time. The sky is quiet again.

Feel the earth beneath you, steady and strong. It has held up these fields for thousands of years. It holds the trees and the stone walls and the sleeping sheep. And tonight, it holds you. You don't need to hold yourself up anymore. Let the ground take all your weight. Let yourself sink, softly, into the earth's patient, steady care.

The earth holds you. The stars watch over you. And the night stretches out, long and calm, with plenty of time for every kind of rest. There's no need to hurry toward morning. It will come all on its own, when it's ready. For now, there's only this soft meadow, and this wide, quiet sky.

show.text: The earth holds you. The stars watch over you.

segments.say: Your breath is very slow now. Your body is warm and heavy. The stars blur gently into one soft glow. The sounds of the night grow distant and dreamy. And you're drifting, slowly, peacefully, out over the quiet fields and into the soft darkness of sleep, where everything is calm and nothing needs doing at all.
